title: Practice: Structure of the Periodic Table

questions.stem: An element is found in Period 3 and Group 6 of the periodic table. Which of the following can you determine about this element?

options.text: It has 3 electron shells and 3 electrons in its outer shell
It has 6 electron shells and 3 electrons in its outer shell
It has 3 electron shells and 6 electrons in its outer shell
It has 6 electron shells and 6 electrons in its outer shell

questions.explanation: The period number tells you the number of electron shells (3 shells), and the group number tells you the number of electrons in the outer shell (6 outer electrons). This element is sulfur (S), with electronic configuration 2,8,6.

questions.stem: A student finds that element X forms an oxide with the formula X₂O₃. In which group of the periodic table is element X most likely found?

options.text: Group 1
Group 2
Group 3
Group 6

questions.explanation: In X₂O₃, oxygen has a valency of 2 (needing 2 electrons), so 3 oxygens need 6 electrons in total. Two atoms of X provide these 6 electrons, meaning each X atom loses 3 electrons. Elements that lose 3 electrons to form ions with a 3+ charge are found in Group 3.

questions.stem: Elements A and B are in the same group but different periods. Elements B and C are in the same period but different groups. Which pair is most likely to have similar chemical properties?

options.text: B and C, because they are in the same period
A and C, because they are in different groups and periods
A and B, because they are in the same group
All three elements have identical properties

questions.explanation: Elements in the same group have the same number of outer shell electrons, which determines their chemical properties. Elements in the same period have the same number of electron shells but different numbers of outer electrons, so they have different chemical properties.

questions.stem: A teacher shows students an element that is a poor conductor of electricity and forms negative ions. Where on the periodic table is this element most likely located?

options.text: On the left side, in Groups 1 or 2
In the middle, among the transition metals
On the right side, in Groups 6 or 7
At the bottom of Group 1

questions.explanation: Non-metals are found on the right side of the periodic table. They are poor conductors of electricity and tend to gain electrons to form negative ions. Elements in Groups 6 and 7 gain 2 or 1 electrons respectively to achieve a full outer shell.

questions.stem: The periodic table shows a stepped line separating metals from non-metals. Germanium sits on this line. Which prediction about germanium's properties is most reasonable?

options.text: It will be a very reactive metal that explodes in water
It will be a gas at room temperature
It may have properties of both metals and non-metals, such as being a semiconductor
It will be completely inert like the noble gases

questions.explanation: Elements that sit on the boundary between metals and non-metals (called metalloids or semi-metals) often display properties of both. Germanium is a well-known semiconductor, conducting electricity under some conditions but not others, making it valuable in electronic components.
